summary: Owen County lookout built in 1949 on what is now Owen-Putnam State Forest land; the tower is gone, but four concrete bases remained in April 2024.

facts.status_note: Not standing. All four concrete tower bases still exist on the site (April 2024 visit).
facts.agency: Indiana Department of Natural Resources, Division of Forestry (Owen-Putnam State Forest)

access.note: State forest land in Owen-Putnam State Forest. The DNR recreation guide lists hiking and bridle trails, hunting and fishing across the forest.

visit.trail_note: No source I could read describes how visitors reach the old footings.

events.note: Site land bought October 24, 1948 (13.06 acres, $391); footers dug in 1948.
Tower constructed in 1949. A November 1949 newspaper item called it Indiana's 24th fire tower.
April 2024 visit: tower not standing; all four concrete bases remained.

evidence.supports: land bought October 1948, 13.06 acres; footers dug 1948; tower constructed 1949
evidence.quote: The footers were dug in 1948. The tower was constructed in 1949.
The land at this site was purchased on 10/24/1948; 13.06 acres purchased from Billy Martin for $391.

evidence.quote: Indiana's 24th fire tower is near completion in Owen county

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record says Owen State Forest. Indiana Fire Towers places the site in Owen-Putnam State Forest and says Owen State Forest was created in July 1937. The current name is used in the story.

sources.title: Lookout Towers
sources.publisher: U.S. Forest Service, Hoosier National Forest

notes_for_editor: The removal date was not found in any source read, so the story does not give one. Build year 1949 is supported by two sources. Do not confuse this with the McCormick's Creek tower in Owen County, which the firelookout list marks as standing. The Forest Service list gives Cloverdale as the nearest town; Indiana Fire Towers gives Upper Cataract Falls as the location.
